title: Safe Navigation and Conditional Evaluation
subtopics: Choosing between safe navigation, guards, and explicit conditions
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of safe navigation and conditional evaluation in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply safe navigation and conditional evaluation in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to choosing between safe navigation, guards, and explicit conditions and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Safe Navigation and Conditional Evaluation through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding safe navigation and conditional evaluation helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Safe Navigation and Conditional Evaluation helps you reason about the safe-navigation operator &.. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: The safe-navigation operator &.. Then connect it to Nil-aware method calls. The remaining syllabus points—Choosing between safe navigation, guards, and explicit conditions—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain safe navigation and conditional evaluation, identify its place in data types, literals, and operators, run a focused example, and verify an important boundary. Revisit the linked exercise if this is a core topic; advanced runtime or framework examples remain draft until reviewed in a suitable environment.
